author: BBC News
description:
China appears determined to acquire America’s most advanced computing technology – but how far might it go to get it?

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has publicly acknowledged having an affair, amid reports raising questions about whether the woman involved had links to Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia’s board said it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security have been compromised, though it’s launched an independent investigation into the matter. The revelations have also raised broader questions about China’s longstanding efforts to acquire American technology, including through espionage.
On The Global Story, host Asma Khalid speaks to Randy Schriver and Mike Kuiken of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission about the national security implications – and what the Nvidia scandal could mean for America’s approach to selling advanced chips to China. title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bigger than you think | The Global Story

description:
Negotiations to end the war in Ukraine have intensified, after a nine month gap. President Donald Trump's envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff took part in talks with Russian and Ukrainian and representatives in Abu Dhabi at the weekend - which Mr Kushner described as productive. The Americans have now met Vladimir Putin in Moscow, where they proposed expanding talks to include European leaders. Next, Mr Witkoff and Mr Kushner will travel to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at a summit of the European Political Community. 

But, in spite of all these meetings, has any real progress been made towards peace? 

In this video we speak to our Russia editor Steve Rosenberg in Moscow about the Kremlin's territory demands, and ask our Ukraine analyst Vitaly Shevchenko what he makes of the latest talks.

author: BBC News
description:
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of tech giant Nvidia, the company's board says, with chief financial officer Colette Kress appointed interim boss.
 
The resignation was announced in the wake of affair with suspected Chinese spy, which led to the firm's stocks plunging.
 
The company's shares have recovered some ground after initially plummeting more than 13% when US markets opened shortly after news of Huang's resignation.

On Sunday, Huang admitted an affair with a woman who was repeatedly from another company and suspected to be a Chinese spy. On Thursday, the New York Times reported that he had a second affair with an executive at his own company.

description:
The board of tech giant Nvidia is considering whether to oust its CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with a woman, reportedly from another company - who is also allegedly a Chinese spy.
 
Allegations of a second affair have since been reported by the New York Times with an executive at his own company.
 
Since then, Nvidia’s share price has plunged by nearly 8%, wiping hundreds of billions of dollars off the value of the AI chip giant.
 
Beijing has warned the US not to use the spying allegations as a pretext to once again restrict tech sales to China. Nvidia is investigating the affair Huang has admitted, as is the FBI.

author: BBC News
description:
More than 300,000 people in the UK are living with Tourette syndrome - a neurological disorder that can cause sudden, involuntary and repetitive movements and sounds known as tics.
 
According to Tourette's Action, it affects one in every hundred children. A new device designed to help calm their tics, could make a huge difference in their lives. 
 
BBC News Correspondent Navtej Johal has followed the journey of this gadget for years as it was developed using research from the University of Nottingham.
 
He meets teenagers struggling with Tourette’s who say the device, which looks like a smartwatch, has been “life-changing”.

description:
Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades.
 
Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years.
 
Only a few thousand votes separated Colom from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.
